newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Algeria hopes to invest in Portuguese natgas.
newsitem.headline: Algeria hopes to invest in Portuguese natgas.

text.p: Algeria and Portugal are discussing possible investment by the former's state oil and gas company Sonatrach in natural gas distribution in Portugal, Algerian Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf said.
Last month Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres inaugurated a $1.88 billion pipeline carrying natural gas from Algeria to Portugal via Morocco and Spain.
In Portugal, state gas company Transgas will deliver gas to regional distributors and industrial companies.

"It is an item on our bilateral agenda and Sonatrach has expressed the very strong hope to be a partner with Transgas in the transport and distribution of the natural gas in Portugal," Attaf told a news conference during a visit to Lisbon.

"It is being discussed in terms of conditions, scope and terms of reference, and I am sure that the discussions being held will lead to a satisfactory solution regarding the participation of Sonatrach in gas transport and distribution in Portugal," he added.
Transgas has estimated that Portugal would receive 2,231 million cubic metres of natural gas in 1999 and 2,846 million cubic metres in 2003.
Portugal received no natural gas supplies before the construction of the pipeline was completed last November.
